head: e9e35067fc3b419a54d790a71663071455f203f1
changes: Replace the growable typed-session LRU vector with inline slots for every supported registry key; unused slots are included in the session census.
Keep hit ordering, eviction, clearing and reconfiguration allocation-free at the cache-container level. Cached program payload allocation remains separate.
Bound typed registry inline storage and cap capacities to 64 KiB before identity hashing; reject excess spare capacity without changing accepted identities.
Move the registry into the session and borrow it for typed-worker input verification, removing that worker's duplicate clone.
Check inline Session plus registry backing against a separate 1 MiB allowance and subtract it from active prover RAM; cache reconfiguration cannot consume it.
Reject process configurations that exhaust the session allowance before worker launch; use the same checked active-memory calculation for configuration and sessions.

Keep Rust and Python admission aligned by adding 1 MiB to each registered-program reservation independently of its configured number of live cache entries; batch plans retain their conservative summation.

preliminary_revisions.reason: Compiler rejected iterator temporary borrowing the fixed cache during mutation; compute the hit index before the mutable branch.
One full-size resource fixture retained the old host allowance; updated it and the matching Rust fixture by 1 MiB. Final Python suite passes.
Successful proving qualification before the final caller audit added pre-launch session-budget validation and repaired synthetic worker fixture budgets.
Initial selector used an incorrect module path and ran zero cases; not counted as validation.
Two synthetic cached-worker fixtures reserved only 1000 bytes and failed the new session allowance; their budgets and process fixture budgets now include the session reservation.
The CPU reference-worker lifecycle fixture was selected in a GPU build, whose runtime explicitly rejects that execution mode. The fixture now compiles only in CPU-only builds and is covered there.

Broadened GPU-build process test selection included two existing CPU-reference lifecycle fixtures; they reject GPU builds by design. All eleven process lifecycle cases pass in the CPU build. Final GPU qualification targets the new process-configuration boundary test.
Final source revision, with cached-worker and GPU-build/CPU-build process lifecycle regression coverage.

limitations: Logical ownership census is not RSS and does not establish a throughput improvement. Slot storage conservatively overlaps the per-prover PCS inline census.
Process bootstrap Config retains a separate registry for context rebinding; configuration serialization, incoming requests/results and coordinator lifetimes remain open.
Shared GPU engine/context/accounting, allocator/driver/OS overhead, thread stacks and complete worker/coordinator phase composition remain unqualified.
Ordinary pool admission still rejects profiles missing the complete versioned phase plan; historical descriptors must regenerate the added reservation.
Cache counts 3 and 12 have host coverage. Full-size GPU runs retain one program and do not qualify broader live-cache workloads.
Nonempty-child full-size merges, broader workloads, paired performance comparisons, 24 hours AND 150 completed roots, multiple GPUs and AMD/Metal qualification remain open.
Verification remains on CPU; proof encodings, parameters and proving arithmetic activation are unchanged.
